content.value_statement: Long AI sessions can waste tokens, increase latency, and lose important context. This skill gives practical patterns for compaction, masking, caching, and partitioning.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to compact conversation history near context limits.
Describes how to replace verbose tool outputs with compact references.
Shows cache-friendly ordering for stable prompts and reused templates.
Outlines context partitioning with focused sub-agent work.
Provides budget triggers based on token use, cost, latency, and quality.
limitations: It is guidance, not an automated context management library.
It does not measure token usage inside a live runtime.
It does not guarantee quality preservation after summarization.
It requires project-specific validation before production use.

use_cases.title: Reduce Agent Token Load
use_cases.description: Apply compaction and masking when long tool sessions begin to crowd the context window.

use_cases.title: Plan Production Context Budgets
use_cases.description: Define token budgets for prompts, tools, retrieval, history, and reserved response space.

use_cases.title: Improve Long-Document Workflows
use_cases.description: Partition large research or document tasks into focused contexts before synthesis.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Optimization Method
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a long conversation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this conversation state. Recommend whether I should use compaction, observation masking, caching, partitioning, or no optimization yet.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Context Budget
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for an agent workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a context budget for my workflow. Allocate tokens for system prompt, tools, retrieved documents, message history, and response buffer.

prompt_templates.title: Design Masked Observations
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced handling of verbose tool output
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an observation masking policy for these tool outputs. Define what to keep, summarize, reference, and restore on demand.

prompt_templates.title: Partition a Complex Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Split this large task into isolated sub-agent contexts. Define each context, input, expected output, and final aggregation method.

output_examples.input: A coding agent has many old build logs and a growing chat history.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends masking old build logs, compacting resolved decisions, and preserving the latest failure details.

output_examples.input: A document analysis task exceeds the available context window.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests partitioning documents by topic, summarizing each partition, and merging only validated findings.

output_examples.input: A production prompt changes every request and misses cache benefits.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends stable prompt prefixes, consistent formatting, reused templates, and unique content near the end.

best_practices: Measure token use, latency, and quality before applying optimization.
Keep recent critical observations visible until their purpose is complete.
Test compaction quality against realistic production workloads.
anti_patterns: Do not compress system prompts or active safety instructions.
Do not mask evidence that is still needed for current reasoning.
Do not optimize only for token savings while ignoring output quality.

faq.question: Does this skill increase the model context window?
faq.answer: No. It helps use the available context window more effectively.

faq.question: Can it automatically compact my conversation?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and decision rules that an agent or developer can implement.

faq.question: When should I use compaction?
faq.answer: Use it when context use is high and older material can be summarized without losing key decisions.

faq.question: What is observation masking?
faq.answer: Observation masking replaces verbose tool outputs with compact references and key summaries.

faq.question: Is this useful for Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance applies to Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and similar agent workflows.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation and does not require network access.
